div.l: Wurthy to be Stywardis of Rent and lond
Of eny lord that is in Englond
To make him lyve by his ꝓpropre good
In honure detteles but if he were wood
Or lyue as scarcely as him list desire
And habil forto help alle a Shire
In any case that myght falle or happe
And yit this Maunciple sette ther aldir cappe
¶ The Reve was a sclendre colric man̄
His berd was shaue as nygh as eủer it can̄
His here was by his eris rounde y shorn̄
His toppe was dockid like a prest beforn̄
Ful long were his leggis and ful lene
Y like a staffe ther was no calf y sene ·
Wel coude he kepe a garner ⁊and a Bynne
Ther nas none Auditour coude on him wynne
Wel wist he by the drought ⁊and by the reyne
The yilding of his sede and of his greyne
His lordis Shepe his nete and his deyrye
His Swyne his hors his stede and his pultry
Was hoolly in this Reues goủernyng
And by his couenant yave the rekenyng
Syn that his lord was twenti yere of age
Ther couth no man bringe him in arrerage
Ther ne was bailly hierd neithir hyne
That he ne coude his sleiȝt ⁊and his couuyne
They were a drad of him as of the dethe
His wonyng was feir͗e upon̄ an hethe ·
With grene trees shadowid was his place .
He couth bettir than his lord purchace
Ful riche he was y storid priuely
His lord couth he pleas wel subtily
To yeve ⁊and lene him of his ovne good
And haue a thank and yit a cote and an hode
In youth lerned he had a good mystere
He was a wel good wright a Carpinter͗e
This Reue he sate vpon a wel good Stot
That was pomely grey and hight Scot
A long Surcote of perce vpon he hadde
And by his side he bare a rusty blade
